feedback.summary: The strategy has a strong adaptive core — it reads tendency data, rotates calls, and won the game — but it is bloated with self-contradicting rules and a few outright wrong table reads (notably the blitz/screen and pass_medium/blitz lines). The biggest weakness is that the same tendency (screen-heavy) is mapped to both 'blitz' and 'man' in different places, so the actual calls drifted toward man and got burned. Tightening the matchup table into one authoritative lookup and deleting the contradictory parentheticals would make this a 4-5 strategy.
strengths: Clear priority ordering (situational correctness → counter tendency → keep what works → break predictability) gives a usable decision hierarchy.
Explicit anti-predictability mechanics (35% cap, ban a call after 3 of last 6) are concrete and actionable.
Good situational coverage: 4th-down field-position rules, two-minute drill, and clock-milking are all spelled out.

mistakes.md_issue: Contradiction: 'screen-heavy → blitz' appears in the Defense Rules, but the same section also says 'man is -- vs screen' and later calls use man. The table actually shows screen is ++ vs blitz and -- vs man, so 'screen-heavy → blitz' is simply wrong.
mistakes.fix: Replace with: 'If screen is their top play (>30%): call man (screen is -- vs man). Never blitz a screen-heavy offense — screen is ++ vs blitz.' Delete every 'screen-heavy → blitz' line.

mistakes.what: pass_medium was called into blitz-heavy looks and produced sacks (d70, d82, d89, d103 all strip/sacks on Siroco).
mistakes.md_issue: The .md's own parenthetical admits confusion: 'blitz is -- for pass_medium? no: pass_medium vs blitz is --'. The rule text is garbled and never cleanly states pass_medium is -- vs blitz.
mistakes.fix: Add a clean lookup: 'pass_medium is -- vs blitz and - vs prevent. Never call pass_medium when blitz >30% on the down. vs blitz use screen (++) or pass_short (+).'

mistakes.moment: d11, d157, d162-d164 — prevent/cover3 on 4th down and 3rd & long
mistakes.what: Prevent on 4th & 18 and cover3 on 3rd & 10/4th & 5 let short and medium throws convert; the bot scored on the final drive.
mistakes.md_issue: 'Two-minute (they're driving): prevent to keep everything in front' is too generic and conflicts with the table (prevent is -- vs pass_short and pass_medium, ++ only vs run_inside/pass_deep).
mistakes.fix: Rewrite: 'On 3rd/4th & 7+, if their tendency is pass_short/pass_medium, call man or cover3 (beats short/medium). Use prevent ONLY when their tendency is pass_deep or run_inside.'

mistakes.moment: d2/d3 — play_action on 2nd & 9 and 1st & 10 with only one run logged
mistakes.what: play_action was called at 50% run share but the .md's own threshold is 40%+ established; early play_action vs base was fine, but the rule as written invites overuse before the run is truly established.
mistakes.md_issue: 'Set up play_action — run 40%+ early' is vague about WHEN the 40% is measured (season, last 10 plays, this drive?) and gives no cap on play_action frequency.
mistakes.fix: Add: 'Do not call play_action until you have run on at least 3 of your last 6 plays. Cap play_action at 1 in any 4-play window.'

suggestions: Build ONE authoritative matchup table in the .md and forbid any prose that contradicts it. Half the errors here came from parentheticals that argued with the table.
State each tendency→counter mapping exactly once. Duplicated rules ('screen-heavy → blitz' vs 'man is -- vs screen') create drift; the model picked whichever it read last.
Add explicit 'never call X when Y' negative rules (e.g., never pass_medium vs blitz, never blitz vs screen). Negative constraints are easier to obey than positive heuristics under pressure.
Define measurement windows for every threshold ('40% run', '35% cap', '6+ uses'): say last N plays or this drive, otherwise the model guesses and the rule becomes decorative.

feedback.summary: The plan is readable and the in-game reasoning shows real effort to counter tendencies, but the .md itself is almost entirely platitudes ('play aggressive', 'mix it up', 'be smart') with no concrete if/then rules, so every decision had to be improvised. It also lacks any situational framework for 4th down, clock management, or goal-line defense, which is exactly where the game was lost. The result is a strategy that reads well but gives the bot almost nothing to execute against.
strengths: Clear, positive tone and a coherent high-level philosophy (aggressive offense, balanced play calling) that is easy to follow.
Mentions the key situational buckets (4th down, protecting a lead, mixing calls) so the bot at least knows what topics matter.
Short and readable, so it never contradicts itself outright.

md:
# Adaptive Counter-Punch: "Read the Tendency, Break the Tendency"

## Core Philosophy
Every call is a bet on what the opponent will call. Win the bet by (1) exploiting their revealed tendencies, (2) staying one step ahead of their counter to your tendencies, and (3) never letting any single call exceed ~35% of your play mix. Situational football (down, distance, clock, score) constrains the menu; tendencies pick within it.

## Priority Order (highest first)
1. **Situational correctness** — never violate down/distance/clock/score rules below.
2. **Counter their most-called defense** (from tendency data) with the play that beats it.
3. **Keep what works** — if a call is averaging >5.5 YPP or >50% success over 6+ uses, keep it in the mix (but rotate the counter).
4. **Break predictability** — if any of your calls exceeds 35% of recent plays, force a different call next.
5. **Set up play_action** — run 40%+ early; then play_action becomes a weapon.

## Reading the Tendency Data
- **Overall defense mix**: identify their top call. If one call is >30%, attack its weakness every time it's situationally legal.
- **1st down**: most defenses are conservative (base/cover2/cover3). Attack with the play that beats their 1st-down tendency.
- **3rd & 5+**: expect blitz or man/cover2. If blitz-heavy → screen or pass_medium (blitz is -- for pass_medium? no: pass_medium vs blitz is --; use screen ++ vs blitz, or pass_short + vs blitz). If man-heavy → pass_short is -- vs man; use run_outside ++ vs man or pass_deep ++ vs man.
- **Last plays**: if they just got burned, expect the counter to your last call — call the play that beats that counter.
- **Their offense tendencies** (for your defense): call the coverage that beats their most-used play. If they run inside a lot → cover2/prevent (++). If they pass deep → cover2/prevent (-- for them, good for you). If they blitz-counter... (defense side: pick coverage that is ++ or + vs their top play).

## Offense Rules
- **1st & 10 (own territory)**: default run_inside or pass_short vs base/cover2 tendencies. If they show cover2-heavy → run_inside (++). If cover3-heavy → pass_short (++). If man-heavy → run_outside (++).
- **1st & 10 (opp territory, <40)**: mix pass_medium (++ vs cover2/goal_line) and run_outside.
- **2nd & short (<4)**: run_inside or qb_sneak vs prevent/cover2; play_action if run established.
- **2nd & long (>7)**: pass_medium vs cover2/goal_line; pass_deep vs man; screen vs blitz.
- **3rd & short (<3)**: qb_sneak (++ vs prevent, + vs cover2/man) unless they show goal_line/blitz → run_inside or pass_short.
- **3rd & 5+**: counter their 3rd-down tendency: blitz→screen; man→pass_deep or run_outside; cover2→pass_medium or run_inside; cover3→pass_short; prevent→run_inside or qb_sneak.
- **Red zone / goal line**: play_action (++ vs base/goal_line), pass_medium (++ vs cover2/goal_line), run_inside (++ vs cover2/prevent). Avoid pass_deep vs cover2/prevent.
- **4th down**:
  - 4th & ≤2, past opponent 40 → go for it (qb_sneak/run_inside).
  - 4th & ≤3, opponent 35–45, trailing or tied → go for it.
  - In FG range (opponent ≤35) and 4th & >3 → kick FG.
  - 4th & >3 outside FG range → punt, unless trailing by >10 in Q4 → go for it.
  - Never go for it on own ≤30 unless 4th & 1 and trailing late.
- **Two-minute drill (end of half, trailing)**: pass_medium/pass_deep/screen, spike/kneel logic: if <10s and not in FG range, pass_deep; if in FG range, kick.
- **Protecting lead (Q4, +7 or more, <5 min)**: run_inside/run_outside/qb_sneak heavy, milk clock, avoid incompletions; kneel if <2 min and opponent has no timeouts.

## Defense Rules
- Match coverage to their top offensive tendency: run_inside-heavy → cover2/prevent; run_outside-heavy → man/prevent; pass_short-heavy → cover3; pass_medium-heavy → cover2/goal_line; pass_deep-heavy → man/goal_line; screen-heavy → blitz; play_action-heavy → base/goal_line.
- **1st down**: base or cover2 (safe vs run and short pass).
- **3rd & long**: blitz or cover2 (blitz -- vs pass_medium? blitz is -- for pass_medium, so blitz good vs pass_medium; but pass_deep + vs blitz). If they pass deep on 3rd long → man/goal_line. If they check down → blitz.
- **3rd & short**: goal_line or base to stop run/sneak.
- **Red zone**: goal_line or cover2.
- **Two-minute (they're driving)**: prevent to keep everything in front, but if they dink-and-dunk, switch to man/blitz.
- **Never call same coverage >35% of recent plays.**

## Anti-Predictability
- Track your own last 6 calls; if any call appears 3+ times, ban it for the next 2 plays.
- After a big gain, expect their counter: call the play that beats the counter to your last call (e.g., last was pass_short vs cover3 → they'll play man → run_outside or pass_deep).
- Rotate between two "families" (run-heavy series, then pass-heavy series) so tendencies stay balanced.

## Examples
**Example 1 — 3rd & 7, opponent shows 45% blitz on 3rd & 5+.** Screen is ++ vs blitz. Call **screen**. If they'd shown man-heavy instead, call **pass_deep** (++ vs man).

**Example 2 — 1st & 10, own 30, opponent overall 40% cover2.** Run_inside is ++ vs cover2. Call **run_inside**. Next play, they'll likely counter with base/blitz (run_inside is - / -- there); call **pass_medium** (++ vs cover2, + vs base) or **screen** (++ vs blitz) to stay ahead.

## Clock & Score
- Trailing by 2 scores in Q4: hurry-up, pass_medium/deep, go for it on 4th & ≤4 past midfield.
- Leading by 1 score, <4 min: run-heavy, punt on 4th & >2 unless past opponent 40.
- Tied, <1 min, in FG range: run to center, kick FG.
- Overtime: score-first mentality; on defense, blitz/man to force a stop; on offense, play_action and pass_medium.

# The Simple Game Plan: Play Hard, Play Smart

- Play aggressive on offense and try to move the ball down the field.
- Mix up the play calling so the defense can't guess what's coming.
- Run the ball sometimes and pass the ball sometimes to keep things balanced.
- On defense, be ready for anything and don't let them make big plays.
- Be smart on fourth down and take the points when you can.
- Protect the lead late and don't make silly mistakes.
